body:
I wonder why it works for  `--implements` within guard creation. Maybe the magic is hidden in the `schema.d.ts` which is unfortunately not checked in. But there are two things imported here: https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/blob/9.0.x/packages/schematics/angular/guard/index.ts#L25
Would you mind to share the content of `schema.d.ts`?

Okay, I just forked the angular-cli project and built it locally. The schema produced for the guard seems to look basically like this:

```ts
export interface Schema {
    ...
    implements?: Implement[];
   ...
}

export enum Implement {
    CanActivate = "CanActivate",
    CanActivateChild = "CanActivateChild",
    CanDeactivate = "CanDeactivate",
    CanLoad = "CanLoad",
}
```

I tried to copy the schema and implementation into a very simple example repo:
https://github.com/d-koppenhagen/ngx-multi-select-schematic

But the result will be the same as described in the original issue text. Probably it's a bug and not just a not documented feature?

# 🐞 Bug report ### Command (mark with an `x`) - [ ] new - [ ] build - [ ] serve - [ ] test - [ ] e2e - [x] generate - [x] add - [ ] update - [ ] lint - [ ] xi18n - [ ] run - [ ] config - [ ] help - [ ] version - [ ] doc ### Is this a regression? No, it's not. Multi select prompt is just supported within angular cli > `9.0.0-rc.3`. ### Description Creating an angular schematic that prompts the user for multiple options is possible since https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/issues/16104. labels.name: target: patch

issue.body:
**docs: add how to pass array options to the CLI**
With this change we add an example on how to use array options in the CLI.

Closes #33851


**docs: update CLI command-language syntax**
Remove reference to camel case options and arguments as this is no longer valid in version 14.

Also, wrap required arguments with `<>` as this is correct syntax to differentiate between optional and required args.
